name: Multila
editorial_article: Multila, released in 2000 on the legendary Chain Reaction imprint, stands as a defining monument of the turn-of-the-millennium dub techno scene. Orchestrated by Finnish visionary Sasu Ripatti under his Vladislav Delay moniker, the record originally functioned as a compilation of two earlier EPs—'Huone' and 'Ranta'—which had been released by the label in 1999 and 2000. Despite its functional origins as a collection, Multila possesses a singular, cohesive sonic identity that transcends its parts, establishing it as one of the most significant works in Ripatti's prolific career. \n\nThe album is celebrated for its dense, atmospheric, and highly textural exploration of minimal and dub-infused techno. It balances shorter, hauntingly ambient pieces with the colossal, 22-minute centerpiece "Huone," an odyssey that exemplifies the meticulous, glitch-laden production technique that would come to define the Vladislav Delay sound. By weaving elements of IDM, glitch, and dub-techno into a cold, immersive landscape, Ripatti pushed the boundaries of the Chain Reaction sound, creating a work that remains deeply influential. Decades later, its impact continues to resonate, notably cited by artists such as Animal Collective as a significant influence, further cementing its status as a timeless classic within experimental electronic music. Its legacy is preserved through periodic reissues, including a 2020 remaster by Rashad Becker, ensuring that its intricate, shifting layers remain accessible to new listeners.
